claims.text: Home energy social comparison reports increase social welfare in the evaluated sample.
Traditional evaluation approaches overstate welfare gains from nudges because they ignore significant costs incurred by nudge recipients.
Home energy report welfare gains might be overstated by $620 million overall under traditional evaluations.
Applying a prediction algorithm for optimal targeting would double the welfare gains of the nudge intervention.

evidence.description: "In our sample, the reports increase social welfare, although traditional evaluation approaches overstate gains because they ignore significant costs incurred by nudge recipients."
"...traditional evaluation approaches overstate gains because they ignore significant costs incurred by nudge recipients."
"Overall, home energy report welfare gains might be overstated by $620 million."
"We develop a prediction algorithm for optimal targeting; this approach would double the welfare gains."

methodologies.name: Social Welfare Evaluation Framework for Nudges
methodologies.description: Combines a field experiment with a theoretical framework to evaluate the social welfare impacts of home energy social comparison reports, incorporating recipient costs.
datasets: Home energy social comparison reports field experiment

methodologies.name: Prediction Algorithm for Optimal Targeting
methodologies.description: Predictive targeting approach designed to assign nudge interventions selectively to maximize welfare gains.

limitations.text: Nudge-style interventions are rarely subjected to full social welfare evaluations.
Traditional evaluation approaches ignore significant costs incurred by nudge recipients.
